protocolCritique.reason: Coordinates are zero-based full-original source-pixel centers, x right/y down; phi is radians; widths, lateral offsets, station positions and native longestGap are image pixels, not world lengths. Luminance is arithmetic mean of stored R,G,B levels, not linear-light physical luminance or alpha. u=[24,-5]/sqrt601 and n=[5,24]/sqrt601 give the declared phi and +6n origin to floating precision. No crop or resizing is mathematically needed.
protocolCritique.guard: Do not convert literal bank widths into calibrated physical width or replace original-frame coordinates by crop coordinates. Stored RGB/decoder identity and caller geometry are provenance inputs, not human annotation truth.

protocolCritique.reason: Station centers are before -24..-9, core -8..7, after8..23 and long -24..23. Counts are16/16/16/48; mean station t is -16.5/-0.5/15.5/-0.5, so core and long are not centered at t=0 as discrete point sets. Profile averages those centers without tangent smoothing. Contrast, including loss's internal contrast, averages tangent offsets -2,-1,0,1,2. Its sample-center longitudinal supports are respectively[-26,-7],[-10,9],[6,25],[-26,25]. Neighboring short-window footprints overlap despite disjoint center lists. Bilinear raster sampling adds the surrounding source-pixel interpolation footprint.
protocolCritique.guard: Retain this phase and support exactly; do not recenter, clamp tangent samples at each window boundary or call the short windows independent replicates. Width50 contrast reaches normal offsets±28; loss RGB/background sampling reaches±50; profile reaches±30. Same station labels do not mean identical pixel support across queries.

protocolCritique.reason: The public profile has241 offsets -30..30 step0.25. edgePair requires ok>=max(8,0.2*nT), hence at least8 retained stations for short windows and10 for long; at least145 of241 lateral offsets must be good. It interpolates deficient lateral offsets, applies five-tap lateral smoothing, differentiates in lum/px, and zeros six endpoint gradient bins plus bad bins. Candidate width±2 and midpoint±12 tests occur on discrete peaks before subpixel refinement; returned wPx/cPx are not post-refinement guaranteed to remain within exactly those tolerances.
protocolCritique.guard: Keep nominal width and fitted width distinct. A finite fit is a maximized compatible rising/falling pair, not a physical edge ownership certificate. Preserve conditions and native fitted values; do not silently reject/refit refined outputs against a newly introduced tolerance. The finite lateral aperture and endpoint suppression can remove same-edge candidates, especially the width50 offset control; do not widen the profile after seeing this.

protocolCritique.reason: For the same physical coordinate, O'=O+6n implies local lateral offset r'=r-6. Thus the preregistered midpoint residual cOffset-cPrimary+6 has the correct sign. It is meaningful only for matched window and literal width with both native fits finite, and even then same-edge association is a hypothesis, not a fact. The shifted profile covers original-frame lateral support[-24,36], not the original[-30,30]; midpoint restriction and edge aperture also shift in the original frame. Competing peaks or support truncation can change the selected pair.
protocolCritique.guard: Retain residuals without a new pass tolerance, never infer/recenter from cPx, and preserve both fit objects/conditions. Null or changed peaks retain association UNKNOWN; a small residual alone does not prove semantic or physical-edge identity. The floating origin discrepancy from exact O+6n is only about3e-14px in each coordinate and is not a new scientific tolerance.

protocolCritique.reason: The explicit full-frame binary strip is a caller visibility intervention, not an observed gap. Native bilinear mask>0.01 can hide neighboring fractional sample locations; it is not exactly six missing station centers or a nearest-neighbor six-pixel gap. Each contrast inside/outside band has25 sample positions (five lateral by five tangent); strict minimum visible fraction>0.5 means at least13 retained samples in both bands on each side. A finite contrast with invalid flag is possible; invalid must not be rewritten as NaN, zero or failure. Loss edge visibility requires both side flags; overlay visibility additionally follows its distinct center/background rules.
protocolCritique.guard: Keep null masks distinct from explicit planes, retain every contrast and validity flag, and preserve native visible counts separately for edge and overlay. A masked/invalid station terminates a native visible-failure run; zero visibleCount with longestGap0 is UNKNOWN, not continuity. No missingness mechanism, physical occlusion or gap length is inferred.

protocolCritique.reason: Public profile converts its NaN means to null before the runner sees them; source counts preserve available support but the codec cannot recover discarded runtime NaN identity. Public stationContrast arrays preserve raw NaN and any nonfinite values alongside flags; ordinary JSON would collide NaN/Infinity with null. Native loss intentionally nulls invalid edge minima and rounds many diagnostics to0.001; its native answer, not invented unrounded values, is authoritative. profile:null selects the WHITE-overlay brightness proxy, not fitted path alpha; threshold:null leaves overlay pass/loss/gap/agreement outcomes null.
protocolCritique.guard: Use the accepted tagged codec before JSON serialization, retaining NaN/±Infinity/-0/null distinctly wherever they reach the public answer. Never zero-fill, bridge invalid plotted values, unround native diagnostics, recover discarded hidden sample data, label RGB brightness as opacity, or infer an overlay decision from historical tau8.

protocolCritique.reason: registerQueries resolves top-level string argument values as Part references and memoizes each fn plus JSON.stringify(rawArgs) within its local answers Map. Exact query arguments therefore contain only the raster and mask reference strings, not metadata identifiers. A fresh base:null PartStore and registration map per group/window with all widths sharing that store admits one lazily produced combined constant; literal null is the mask Part's resolved value for unmasked groups. The constant callback can complete before its parent profile callback, so completion order differs from seq order.
protocolCritique.guard: Preserve planned caller order, raw arguments, native unit/value/emits, actual callbacks and native seq/parent/depth. Do not eagerly materialize Parts, sort/renumber callback records, equate query native key/cached fields with returned emits, or fill160/176 into observed counters. Source freeze and an independently reviewed runner must verify actual route behavior before producer admission.

protocolCritique.reason: Long48 reuses the exact union of the three short center lists. At fixed group/width, its contrast station values are the same pointwise transformations represented across the shorts; loss per-station values also reuse these centers, though aggregate gap runs can join across short-window boundaries. An unmasked long profile equals the average of three short profiles up to accumulation rounding; with masking it is a per-offset valid-count-weighted combination, not an unweighted mean of available means. All channels share the original image, selected geometry and related RGB transformations.
